title.rendered: Decreeing Morning and Night: His Mercies Are New Every Morning | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 13

excerpt.rendered: Mercies in the morning, faithfulness in the night. Day 13 teaches a rhythm of daily declaration from Lamentations 3 and Psalm 92.

content.rendered:
God wrapped His people with mercies in the morning and faithfulness in the night. Declaration is how we open both parcels on time.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, October 30, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 13

Today’s Scripture

“Through the Lord’s mercies we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness.”
Lamentations 3:22-23 (NKJV)

“It is good to give thanks to the Lord, and to sing praises to Your name, O Most High; to declare Your lovingkindness in the morning, and Your faithfulness every night.”
Psalm 92:1-2 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Lamentations 3 is a strange, beautiful book. Jeremiah is weeping over a destroyed Jerusalem, and in the middle of the ashes he suddenly remembers: “His mercies are new every morning.” The NKJV is bracing; the AMPC deepens the comfort: “It is because of the Lord’s mercy and loving-kindness that we are not consumed, because His [tender] compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great and abundant is Your stability and faithfulness.” The TPT renders it: “Lord, your tender mercies and lovingkindness never cease. Your great faithfulness is so beautiful; like beams of light streaming from the dawn, your mercies and compassions arise fresh for us every single morning.”

Psalm 92 pairs that with a rhythm, declare His lovingkindness in the morning and His faithfulness every night. The believer who learns to begin the day and close the day with Scripture discovers, over months, that worry grows thin and faith grows thick. From the first call to prayer in Lagos, to the Northern Line commute in London, to the Angelus bells in Manila, to the matatu-horns of Nairobi and the alvorada of São Paulo, believers are learning that a day framed by declaration is a day in which heaven is given room to work.

Jesus kept this rhythm with the Father. He rose “a long while before daylight” (Mark 1:35) to go to the mountain. He went to a solitary place to pray before every major decision. He slept on a boat in a storm because His day had already been settled with the Father before the storm came. Morning anchors the day; night surrenders it. Declaration is the thread that stitches both ends together.

Start simply. In the morning, open your mouth and name God’s mercy over the fresh page. At night, open your mouth and name God’s faithfulness over the day just lived. Do not wait for feelings; let the words lead. “Great is Your faithfulness” is both a sunrise sentence and a bedtime one.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. God has pre-loaded today with mercy and will cover tonight with faithfulness. Both are already true before you feel either.

Personalise. Tie the morning declaration to the day you are stepping into (that meeting, that journey, that conversation) and the night declaration to the day you are placing in His hands.

Proclaim. “His mercies are new this morning” at sunrise; “Great is Your faithfulness over this day” at bedtime. Short, Scripture-anchored, repeated.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that the mercies of the Lord are new over me this morning, and the faithfulness of the Lord will cover me tonight. His compassions never fail. He has already met me at the door of this day. Great is His faithfulness. I open my mouth before the sun rises to agree with heaven, and I open my mouth before I sleep to give the day back into His hand. Nothing in this day will outrun His mercy; nothing in this night will outrun His keeping. My morning is anchored. My evening is covered. My rest is holy. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
